basis: Defined by central neurodevelopmental impairment and neurologic motor abnormalities; motor findings alone do not establish muscle disease.
Sarcoma arising in the trachea, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Chronic disease of cutaneous apocrine sweat glands.
Palm and sole hyperkeratosis defines this umbrella; systemic manifestations are subtype dependent.
RPGR-related retinal degeneration with progressive visual impairment; no common extraocular damage established.
Multivitamin transport deficiency causes neurodegeneration; hypogammaglobulinemia in 2/2 supports immune dysfunction. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Brain malformations define the disease; despite its historical name, annotated optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Hearing loss and cataracts are below 30%.
Lysosomal encephalopathy; infiltrative liver and spleen enlargement in 2/2. Respiratory insufficiency lacks evidence of direct lung damage; optic atrophy is below 30%.
Adenocarcinoma of the periampullary duodenal region; biliary ancestry alone does not establish hepatic origin or damage.
PROM1-related retinal degeneration with severe visual loss and macular degeneration.
Congenital aortic valve obstruction causes cardiac dysfunction; dyspnea does not establish direct lung disease.
Marrow plasma cell neoplasm; destructive bone disease in most and direct paraprotein-associated renal injury in at least 30%. Neuropathy is below 30%.
Autonomic movement disorder; repetitive diaphragm contractions do not establish muscle injury. Dehydration and malnutrition do not establish direct endocrine disease.
Skeletal dwarfism and microcephaly/ID define the syndrome; glaucoma and dental enamel defects/agenesis each occur in 30-79%. Sparse hair omitted under the cap.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the esophagus; cough and voice changes do not establish direct airway injury. Toe anomalies are not characteristic of this cancer.
Immune-mediated cutaneous lichen planus with annular lesions; common oral involvement is not established for this variant.
Sparse record identifies short stature and contractures as defining locomotor abnormalities; hypotonia alone does not establish neurologic disease.
Developmental impairment and ptosis define the syndrome; talipes in 50%, joint hypermobility in 60%, and vertebral fusion in 30% support musculoskeletal involvement.
Large cerebral artery occlusion causes ischemic brain injury; both arterial disease and brain injury define the concept.
Immune-mediated inflammation of lung parenchyma from inhaled antigens; absence of fibrosis does not remove pulmonary involvement.
Cataracts, congenital septal heart defects, and neural tube defects with tethered cord define the syndrome. Joint limitation lacks a qualifying frequency.
Malformations of neuronal migration are structural developmental disorders of the brain.
NLRP3-related cochlear autoinflammation causes hearing loss, sometimes without systemic inflammation. Other inflammatory manifestations lack qualifying frequencies or lasting damage.
Metaplastic lesion located in urinary bladder urothelium; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Functional gastric disorder with impaired digestion; listed potential causes do not establish additional organ involvement.
